architecture.mechanism: Holding control — deliberately delaying buses at stops (or combining holding with other measures) so that buses on the same route do not travel closely together, thereby regularizing headways.
architecture.intervention: Deploy an AVL/APC-driven holding scheme on the existing fleet: when a bus runs ahead of its predecessor's headway target, hold it at time-point stops (and combine with minor speed adjustment of the trailing bus) to enforce even spacing — no additional buses required.
architecture.expected_effect: Evenly spaced arrivals and reduced bunching (fewer "three buses together, then nothing" events), lower headway variance, and shorter average commuter waiting time without fleet expansion.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the holding controller on one trial route for a set period while a comparable route stays uncontrolled; measure headway variance, bunching-incident count, and mean passenger wait before/after — if the trial route shows no statistically significant reduction in headway variance and bunching versus the control, the mechanism is falsified.
